program_name: Quantitative Finance and Insurance (Master Program in Quantitative Finance and Insurance / Finanza Quantitativa e Assicurazioni) - UNITO internal degree-programme code [2305M21], apply.unito.it course id 288, en.unito.it degree id 32498. The programme was drafted elsewhere as 'Finance'; 'Quantitative Finance and Insurance' is the official name.
level: master (second-cycle degree / Laurea Magistrale, 2 years, 120 ECTS, full-time; UNITO's own pages call it 'Type of course: second cycle degree' and apply.unito.it lists 'Type: POSTGRADUATE DEGREE, full-time')
teaching_language: Case 1 - fully English-taught. The entire degree is delivered in English; apply.unito.it lists 'Study language: English' and the UNITO catalogue lists teaching language English. It is a single-university UNITO degree run by the Department of Economics, Social Studies, Applied Mathematics and Statistics (ESOMAS) within the School of Management and Economics - NOT an interuniversity/joint degree and NOT an English pathway inside an Italian-named degree. The programme is internally structured into curricula (Finance / Insurance and Statistics), but all curricula are taught in English, so the choice of curriculum does not change the language of instruction. No Italian-language component is required for admission or graduation.
campus: Turin (Torino), Italy. Teaching seat: Torino. Department: Dipartimento di Scienze Economico-Sociali e Matematico-Statistiche (ESOMAS - Department of Economics, Social Studies, Applied Mathematics and Statistics). School: Scuola di Management ed Economia (School of Management and Economics).
degree_class: LM-83 - Scienze statistiche attuariali e finanziarie (Actuarial and Financial Statistics / Statistical, Demographic and Actuarial Sciences). AlmaLaurea records the programme as 'LM-83, ex LM-16', i.e. it was previously classified under LM-16 (Finanza) and is now LM-83. UNITO internal programme code: 2305M21. Graduates of this LM-83 degree have access to the Italian State exam for the qualification of Actuary (Attuario).
admission_type: Open access (accesso libero / 'course without restricted number of places' - apply.unito.it and en.unito.it both list access as 'Free'), BUT admission is not automatic: a documented admission application must be submitted within the published windows and is evaluated by a selection committee. In practice it is a curriculum-based (documents + possible interview) selection rather than a numerus clausus with a ranked entrance exam. There is no TOLC, no SAT and no written admission test. Applicants who meet all the automatic-admission thresholds are admitted directly; all others are assessed through an admission interview. International applicants (any citizenship holding a foreign degree) apply through the Apply@UniTo portal; applicants holding an Italian degree apply through separate domestic rounds on the programme's own site. A territorial cap exists only for one group: 50 places are reserved for non-European applicants residing abroad.
application_deadline_eu: A.Y. 2026/27. Two routes: (a) EU/Italian applicants holding a FOREIGN degree apply via Apply@UniTo in the Fourth admission call - 25 August to 8 September 2026, deadline 8 Sept 2026, 23:59:59 CET (this call is 'reserved to Italians, EU and EU equivalents, non-EU citizens legally residing in Italy'); feedback around the beginning of October 2026. They may alternatively use the earlier first call closing 29 January 2026, which is open to all. (b) Applicants of any citizenship holding or about to obtain a degree from an ITALIAN university apply in the programme's domestic rounds: Round 1, 1 April - 31 May 2026 (feedback 18 June 2026) and Round 2, 4 June - 22 August 2026 (feedback 11 September 2026). Chances of admission do not differ between rounds.
application_deadline_non_eu: A.Y. 2026/27: 29 January 2026 - non-EU applicants residing abroad must apply through Apply@UniTo in the First admission call, 25 November 2025 to 29 January 2026, which is the only 2026/27 call 'open to any international student' for postgraduate programmes. The later calls (8 Sept 2026 fourth call) are explicitly reserved to Italians, EU/EU-equivalents and non-EU citizens legally residing in Italy, so non-EU applicants abroad cannot use them. Rolling evaluation batches announced by the programme: feedback around mid-February 2026 for applications completed by 1 January 2026; around mid-March 2026 for applications completed by 24 January 2026; around the beginning of May 2026 for applications completed by 29 January 2026. Note: successful non-EU applicants must additionally complete visa pre-enrolment on the Universitaly platform by the national deadline, which is not stated on the programme pages. [uncertain - Universitaly pre-enrolment date not confirmed on an accessible official page for this programme]
entry_exam_or_test: No written entrance examination and no standardised test (no TOLC, no GMAT/GRE, no SAT). Selection is by document assessment plus, where needed, an ADMISSION INTERVIEW. 'The admission results are decided by a selection committee and none of its members can individually decide about the admission of any student.' Applicants who satisfy every automatic-admission threshold (credits, final mark, grade averages, English B2 certificate) are admitted automatically without interview. 'Students who do not satisfy all the above requirements can be interviewed for admission. The purpose of the interview is to assess whether the applicant masters the tools and knowledge included in QFI Reference Background file, with particular emphasis on mathematics and statistics and whether he/she is motivated to pursue the master course. Applicants who do not show up at the interview will not be admitted. Interviews can be done online.' Separately, apply.unito.it states that English proficiency at B2 'will be verified during the admission interview', implying that international applicants are in practice normally interviewed even when documentation looks complete. Optional (non-selective) preparation: two intensive crash courses in Mathematics and Probability in the first two weeks of September before official classes start - not compulsory but highly recommended. [uncertain - whether an interview is universal for international applicants or only for those missing an automatic-admission threshold; the two official sources word this differently]
academic_requirements:
ENTRY QUALIFICATION: a first-cycle degree (bachelor's / Laurea Triennale) obtained after at least 3 years of university education, or an equivalent or higher title. Applicants who do not yet hold the degree at application time may apply provided they can obtain it no later than the final enrolment deadline (typically by the end of the following December).

QUANTITATIVE BACKGROUND (minimum prerequisite): the previous studies must include at least 15% of credits (27 CFU for Italian degrees) in one or more of the following areas: Mathematics (MAT/*), Statistics and Mathematical Methods for Decisions (SECS-S/*), Econometrics (SECS-P/05), Computer Science (INF/01, ING-INF/*). These credits may be accumulated over several previous programmes (e.g. a bachelor's plus a master's) and may include certified single exams taken in addition to the degree. Applicants who do not meet this prerequisite are told to take and certify individual courses in those areas before applying. NOTE: apply.unito.it phrases the same 15% requirement over the areas 'Mathematics, Statistics and Mathematical Methods for Decisions, Econometrics, Computer Science', and adds a broader alternative screening criterion for its own applicant pool: 'We will consider all the applicants who satisfy at least one of the following criteria: i) first-cycle degree issued from an Institution in the top 12.5% of the RePEc ranking of the Economics departments; ii) final grade greater or equal to 9.5/10 of the highest possible grade (for example, 105/110 for an Italian degree).'

AUTOMATIC ADMISSION (no interview) requires ALL of: 18 CFU/ECTS in Mathematics; 18 CFU/ECTS in Economics or Econometrics or Investments or Capital Markets or Corporate Finance or Accounting or Management; 12 CFU/ECTS in Statistics; final graduation mark of at least 105/110 (9.54/10); average grade in Mathematics exams of at least 27/30 (9/10); average grade in Statistics exams of at least 27/30 (9/10); average grade in Economics exams (Microeconomics, Macroeconomics and Econometrics only) of at least 27/30 (9/10); and a certificate of English at B2 or above. Applicants missing any of these are routed to the admission interview (assessed against the 'QFI Reference Background' document, with emphasis on mathematics and statistics, plus motivation).

QUOTA: the programme has no overall numerus clausus (open access), but 'This degree program has 50 available places for non-European applicants residing abroad' (territory requirement on apply.unito.it). No overall cap and no EU sub-quota is published.

STRUCTURE: 2 years, 120 ECTS, full-time; enrolment status (full-time or part-time) may be chosen each year, with tuition adjusted accordingly. Curricula: Finance, and Insurance and Statistics. [uncertain - the exact current curriculum names/number could not be re-verified on a live official page]
language_requirements: ENGLISH ONLY - no Italian language requirement (the degree is fully English-taught, so UNITO's CLIQ Italian B2 rule for Italian-taught programmes does not apply). Required level: B2 (Common European Framework) or above. Two official formulations: (1) the programme's own 'How to apply' page lists 'certificate of English knowledge equal or above B2 (Common European Standards)' among the requirements that must ALL be met for AUTOMATIC admission without interview; (2) apply.unito.it states under Language requirements: 'English - Your knowledge of the English language (at least B2 level) will be verified during the admission interview.' Read together: a B2 certificate is the documentary route to automatic admission, while applicants without such a certificate can have their English assessed in the admission interview instead. No specific certificate brand or minimum score (IELTS / TOEFL / Cambridge / Duolingo / PTE) is named on any official UNITO page for this programme, and no exemption list (e.g. for prior English-medium degrees or native speakers) is published. apply.unito.it's generic postgraduate documentation note confirms that 'English language certifications' are among the 'additional documents required by some specific postgraduate degree programmes'. [uncertain - no named certificate/score table and no published exemption rule; applicants should confirm with the programme which certificates are accepted]
required_documents:
Submitted through the Apply@UniTo portal (apply.unito.it) for applicants with a foreign degree:
1. Valid identity document / passport (passport for non-EU citizens).
2. First-cycle (bachelor's) degree certificate obtained after at least 3 years of university education, or equivalent/higher qualification - original or certified copy. If the degree is not yet awarded, evidence that it will be obtained by the final enrolment deadline (typically end of the following December).
3. Official academic transcript of records listing exams, credits (CFU/ECTS) and grades, so that the 15%-credit quantitative prerequisite and the credit/grade thresholds (18 CFU Mathematics, 18 CFU Economics-area, 12 CFU Statistics, final mark, subject grade averages) can be verified.
4. Certificates of any additional single exams / individual courses taken to reach the quantitative credit prerequisite.
5. MOTIVATION LETTER in English or Italian - explicitly required ('Other requirements: A motivation letter must be added to your application').
6. English language certificate at B2 or above (documentary route to automatic admission; otherwise English is checked at the interview).
7. Optional but recommended: degree programme syllabus / course descriptions issued by the foreign institution, translated into Italian, English, French or Spanish.
8. Payment of the non-refundable EUR 60 application fee within the deadline of the call (the same amount whether one or two degree programmes are selected).
LANGUAGE OF DOCUMENTS: entry-qualification documents are accepted in English, French, Italian or Spanish; documents issued in any other language must be uploaded together with a certified translation into one of those four languages.
AFTER SUBMISSION: UNITO may request further documents such as a Declaration of Value (Dichiarazione di Valore), a Statement of Verification, or a CIMEA Statement of Comparability; the International Students Office may request additional documentation again at the enrolment stage. Applicants holding an ITALIAN degree do not use Apply@UniTo but the programme's own domestic application rounds and instructions.

uncertainty_notes:
ACCESS PROBLEMS DURING RESEARCH (2026-09-01): (1) apply.unito.it returned HTTP 403 to the WebFetch tool but WAS fully retrievable with a normal browser user-agent via curl - this is the primary verified source for this record and its content is quoted verbatim above. (2) The programme microsite www.finance-insurance.unito.it (host 130.186.x) timed out on every live fetch attempt; its 'How to apply' (last updated 27/02/2026, covering A.Y. 2026-2027) and 'Admission requirements' pages were successfully read through Wayback Machine raw snapshots 20260514040707 and 20260514035351 - i.e. the content is genuinely the current 2026/27 version, captured 14 May 2026, not an outdated archive. (3) en.unito.it and www.unito.it are behind Cloudflare/WAF and returned HTTP 403; content from those hosts is reported from search-engine snippets only and is flagged as such. (4) polito.it (Politecnico di Torino) was correctly excluded as out of scope.

FIELD-LEVEL UNCERTAINTIES: (a) entry_exam_or_test - the two official sources describe the interview differently: the programme page says the interview is for applicants who do NOT satisfy all automatic-admission thresholds, while apply.unito.it says English 'will be verified during the admission interview' as though every Apply@UniTo applicant is interviewed. Applicants should assume an interview is likely. (b) language_requirements - a B2-or-above English certificate is named, but no accepted-certificate list, no minimum IELTS/TOEFL/Duolingo/Cambridge score and no exemption rule (e.g. prior English-medium degree, native speaker) is published on any accessible official page. (c) application_deadline_non_eu - 29 January 2026 is derived by combining the programme page ('between Nov 25, 2025, and Jan 29, 2026 (open to any international student)') with the UNITO-wide call calendar; the Universitaly visa pre-enrolment deadline for 2026/27 is not stated on any programme page. (d) academic_requirements - the number and names of curricula ('Finance' and 'Insurance and Statistics', per one source; 'two curricula', per another) come from snippets and could not be re-verified live; the overall (non-territorial) intake size is not published because the programme is open access, so only the 50-place non-EU-abroad reservation is a hard cap. (e) tuition_or_fees_link - the EUR 156-2,800 range is the a.y. 2025-26 figure explicitly carried on apply.unito.it; the 2026-27 bands were not published on any page reachable in this session. The 'Talents 4 UniTo' scholarship specific to this programme appeared only in a search-result summary and could not be verified on a live official page. (f) There is a minor terminological tension between 'open access / accesso libero / course without restricted number of places' (UNITO's formal classification) and the fact that a documented, committee-evaluated application with possible interview is mandatory - this is normal for Italian LM programmes with 'requisiti curriculari' and is not a data conflict, but it means the programme should NOT be presented as automatic-entry.

RECOMMENDED FOLLOW-UP: re-attempt www.finance-insurance.unito.it/do/home.pl/View?doc=how_to_apply.html from an unrestricted network once the A.Y. 2027-2028 version is published; obtain the 'QFI Reference Background' document referenced by the interview procedure; and confirm the accepted English certificates and 2026-27 fee bands directly with the programme office.
